Denial Resubmission Turnaround

PATTERN 01

BH Claim Sent to Medical Plan Instead of Carve-Out

Patient's mental health coverage is managed by Optum Behavioral Health, separate from their UnitedHealthcare medical plan. Claim submitted to UHC medical. Denied immediately. Resubmitted to UHC. Denied again. No one knows about the carve-out. Sessions go uncollected for months.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX identifies carve-out arrangements at eligibility verification, Optum Behavioral Health, Magellan, Beacon, MHNet and routes every BH claim to the correct entity before submission. Zero carve-out routing denials from the first claim on any PMEX BH client.

PATTERN 02

Therapy Sessions Continue Past Plan Authorization

Aetna authorizes 20 outpatient therapy sessions. Practice tracks sessions manually. Session 21 is provided without a continued care authorization. Payer denies retroactively, sometimes covering 3 to 8 sessions simultaneously. Therapist is left collecting from the patient for sessions the plan should cover.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks authorized session counts per patient per payer per plan year, submits continued care requests with updated clinical documentation 3 sessions before limits, and never allows a session to proceed without active coverage confirmed.

PATTERN 03

Virtual BH Session Submitted With Wrong POS or Missing Modifier

Therapist provides telehealth session from home office (patient home = POS 10). Claim submitted with POS 11 (office) and no telehealth modifier. Commercial payer denies, it cannot reconcile the billing location with the place of service. Pattern repeats on all telehealth claims for months.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX applies POS 10 for patient-home telehealth, POS 02 for facility-based originating sites, and Modifier 95 or GT per payer requirements on every BH telehealth claim. Audio-only visits submitted with FQ modifier where covered. No systematic telehealth denial from POS or modifier error.

PATTERN 04

Payer Denies Ongoing Therapy for Insufficient Clinical Justification

Commercial payer requests concurrent review for patient in week 12 of CBT treatment for depression. Progress notes use subjective language without measurable symptom severity scores, functional outcome measures, or treatment response documentation. Payer denies retroactively from authorization date.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reviews BH progress notes for quantified symptom tracking (PHQ-9, GAD-7, PCL-5), functional outcome documentation, and treatment response language that satisfies commercial payer concurrent review standards before any note is submitted as medical necessity support.

PATTERN 05

Service Billed Under Provider Type Not Covered for That Code

LPC bills 90837 under their own NPI. BCBS plan covers psychotherapy only when provided by psychologists or licensed psychiatrists in that state. Claim denied, credential not recognized for the code billed. Pattern repeats for every LCSW and LPC in the practice until someone identifies the payer credentialing rule.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX maps each payer's behavioral health coverage rules by provider credential type before claims are submitted. When a payer limits coverage to specific credential types, claims are submitted under a qualifying supervisor's NPI with correct incident-to documentation where applicable.

PATTERN 06

Intensive Program Services Denied for Missing Concurrent Review

PHP program submits claims for week 3 of intensive treatment. Commercial payer required weekly concurrent review authorization that was never requested after initial admission authorization. All week 3 sessions denied retroactively. $14,000 in services uncollected.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX Prior Auth tracks PHP and IOP authorization renewal calendars, submits weekly concurrent review requests with current clinical documentation, and alerts the clinical team when authorization is approaching renewal. Zero IOP/PHP authorization gap denials on PMEX-managed BH programs.

A single wrong modifier combination can deny an entire month of telehealth sessions systemically.

THE EDUCATION

What Makes Behavioral Health Billing in the USA So Uniquely Complex

Behavioral health billing combines time-based psychotherapy coding, mental health parity law compliance, telehealth modifier complexity, and carve-out insurance routing into one of the most multi-layered billing specialties in U.S. healthcare.

Behavioral health medical billing covers the process of submitting and managing reimbursement claims for psychotherapy, psychiatric evaluation, medication management, substance abuse treatment, and associated mental health services to U.S. insurance payers. The most fundamental coding distinction: psychotherapy CPT codes are time-based. CPT 90832 is 16 to 37 minutes. CPT 90834 is 38 to 52 minutes. CPT 90837 is 53 minutes or more. Billing the wrong code for the documented session time is both an underpayment and a compliance risk.

The second complexity layer is mental health parity compliance. The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA) requires U.S. insurers to cover mental health and substance use services at parity with medical services. In practice, many payers still impose stricter prior authorization requirements, lower session limits, or narrower provider networks for behavioral health. MHPAEA violations can be appealed but only if someone is tracking parity inconsistencies systematically across your patient panel.

Telehealth billing for behavioral health became a permanent fixture in U.S. healthcare after 2020. Medicare now permanently covers audio-video telehealth therapy with modifier 95 and POS 02. Audio-only coverage varies by payer and state. Many private payers require POS 10 for patient-home telehealth. Applying the wrong modifier or POS code systematically denies every telehealth session submitted that way.

Carve-out plans are a fourth complexity unique to behavioral health: some insurers route behavioral health benefits to a separate managed care organization (Optum/UBH, Magellan, Beacon Health). If you submit a claim to the medical insurer instead of the behavioral health carve-out entity, it will be denied even though the patient appears insured.

THE BIGGEST BILLING RISK IN U.S. BEHAVIORAL HEALTH

Telehealth Parity: The Revenue Lost Every Time a Payer Treats Virtual Sessions Differently

Telehealth billing for behavioral health requires the exact right combination of CPT code, modifier, and place of service for each payer. Medicare uses modifier 95 with POS 02 for audio-video telehealth. Some state Medicaid programs accept audio-only with modifier FQ. Most commercial payers require POS 10 when the patient is at home. Apply the wrong combination and every telehealth session from that date forward is systematically denied.

Mental health parity violations add a second invisible revenue leak. When UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, or BCBS imposes a prior auth requirement for behavioral health sessions that they do not require for medical visits of equivalent intensity, that is a MHPAEA violation. PMEX tracks parity inconsistencies across your patient panel and files parity complaints when patterns are identified turning compliance into recovered revenue.

Carve-out routing errors are the third category. Optum Behavioral Health, Magellan, and Beacon Health each operate as separate entities from the medical plan. PMEX identifies which of your patients have carve-out behavioral health plans and routes claims to the correct entity eliminating denials that most practices never trace back to their actual cause.

Yes. PMEx billing specialists log in to your existing SimplePractice account and manage all billing workflows from inside the platform. You do not need to export data, switch systems, or change how your clinicians document. PMEx reads session notes, submits claims, reconciles ERA files, and tracks authorizations all within your SimplePractice account. Our track record: zero ERA mismatches unresolved per month across our client base. Setup typically takes 3 to 5 business days with no disruption to your clinical workflow.

SimplePractice processes ERA files automatically when payers send standard 835 remittance data. When payers use non-standard adjustment codes, send partial payments, or apply contractual adjustments in unusual formats, SimplePractice cannot auto-post correctly. The claim appears resolved in the system but the balance is actually floating unresolved. PMEx reconciles every ERA line by line against the actual EOB and bank deposit manually decoding any non-standard remittance and resolving every mismatch before month-end.

For Medicare behavioral health telehealth in 2025: modifier 95 with POS 02 when the patient is at a telehealth originating site (clinic), or POS 10 when the patient is at home. For audio-only sessions where covered: modifier FQ. For commercial payers, the correct modifier and POS varies by payer. UnitedHealthcare and Optum often require POS 10 for patient-home telehealth. Aetna, Cigna, and BCBS each have their own rules updated annually. PMEx maintains a payer-specific modifier matrix updated continuously so the correct combination is applied before every claim is submitted.

These psychotherapy CPT codes are time-based. CPT 90832 is individual psychotherapy of 16 to 37 minutes. CPT 90834 is individual psychotherapy of 38 to 52 minutes. CPT 90837 is individual psychotherapy of 53 minutes or more. The session duration must be documented in the clinical note to support the code. Billing 90837 for a 45-minute session is upcoding. Billing 90834 for a 55-minute session is undercoding. PMEx reviews documented session duration before selecting the correct CPT code on every claim.

CPT 90785 is the interactive complexity add-on code for psychotherapy sessions that involve additional clinical complexity such as a third party present during the session, a patient with communication barriers, a mandated client, or care coordination with other clinicians. It adds $20 to $40 in reimbursement per qualifying session and requires only a brief additional note entry documenting the complexity factor. Most behavioral health practices miss it on 60 to 80 percent of qualifying sessions because no one has built the documentation prompt into the session note workflow. PMEx reviews every note for 90785 eligibility and applies it on every qualifying claim.

PMEx tracks prior authorization requirements, session limits, and coverage restrictions by payer for behavioral health versus medical services. When a payer imposes stricter requirements on behavioral health than on equivalent medical services for example, requiring prior auth from session 7 when no auth is required for medical visits that is a MHPAEA parity violation. PMEx documents the violation, files a formal parity complaint with the relevant state insurance commissioner or CMS, and pursues retroactive reimbursement for sessions denied under discriminatory authorization requirements. This is included in the standard PMEx engagement.

We serve U.S. behavioral health practices of every size.

Carve-out plans route behavioral health benefits to a separate managed care organization rather than keeping them within the medical plan. The most common U.S. behavioral health carve-out entities are Optum Behavioral Health (UBH), Magellan Health, and Beacon Health Options. When a patient has a carve-out plan, claims must be submitted to the carve-out entity not the medical plan. Submitting to the wrong payer results in denial with a reason code that many billing teams misread as a coverage issue. PMEx identifies carve-out plans at eligibility verification and routes every claim to the correct entity automatically.

PMEx maintains a real-time authorization tracker for every patient in your practice recording the payer, authorization number, total sessions authorized, sessions used, and expiration date. When a patient reaches two sessions before the limit, a prior authorization renewal request is submitted automatically with the required clinical documentation. The authorization count is visible in your daily dashboard. Authorization-gap denials one of the most common and most avoidable billing problems in behavioral health become impossible under this system.

PMEx works directly inside SimplePractice, Therapy Notes, TheraNest, Valant, Kareo, DrChrono, Epic, Athenahealth, and 30 additional behavioral health EHR and practice management platforms. For SimplePractice specifically, PMEx billing specialists work inside your account no data export, no duplicate entry. For other platforms with API access, PMEx connects directly to the claim data. Integration is live within 3 to 5 business days.

PMEx codes substance abuse services using H-codes (H0001 assessment, H0004 counseling per 15 minutes, H0020 methadone administration) and appropriate ICD-10 F1x codes. For ABA therapy, we apply the correct 0362T, 0373T, 97151, and 97153 codes with behavior technician qualifications documented. Substance abuse and ABA billing each have unique credential and documentation requirements with Medicaid and commercial payers PMEx applies them correctly on every claim.
